points.html: Modern History : Miscellaneous

In 19th century the fear of Russian expansion towards India became the basis of Anglo-Afghan relationships. The Treaty of Turkmenchay (1828 AD) created fear among the British due to the increasing inﬂ uence of Russians. Experts in England called this ‘The Crisis in India.”

North Western passes were the key to entering India. Then it was thought that Afghanistan should be under a friendly government or a government which is in congruence with Britishers. The British "Forward Policy" in 19 th century Afghanistan was a proactive, aggressive strategy designed to establish a buffer state against Russian expansion towards India, particularly during the ﬁ rst Anglo-Afghan War (1839- 42). It was advocated by Lord Auckland. This became the basis of Anglo-Afghan relations.

In 19th century Odisha was hit by a severe famine in 1866-67 AD. An estimated one million deaths took place in Odisha. This famine was described as ‘Sea of Calamity’. Odisha famine emerged decisively in the history of Indian famines because after this a Famine Commission under George Campbell was constituted to look into Famines.

Lord Hastings suppressed the Pindaris. Pindaris were ﬁ rst mentioned at the time of the मुगल साम्राज्य [Mughal Empire] attack on Maharashtra in 1689 AD. In the beginning of 19th century, Pindaris had three main leaders - Chittu, Wasil Muhammad and Karim Khan.
Gandhi and Tilak both toured throughout India and worked for social upliftment. Tilak was the ﬁ rst nationalist leader who worked for establishing close relations with masses at the root level.
G.V . Mavalankar who became the last President of Central Legislative Assembly in 1946 AD was the ﬁ rst speaker to enter the ofﬁ ce wearing a Gandhi cap and not the ‘wig’.
Famous constitutionalist B.R. Ambedkar was born on 14 April, 1891 AD at Mhow (now Dr. Ambedkar Nagar) in M.P. and died on 6 December 1956 AD. He was awarded Bharat Ratna posthumously.

Rabindranath Tagore, also known as Gurudev won a Nobel Prize in literature and was a famous author. He was born on 7 May 1861 AD at Calcutta as son of Debendranath Tagore and Sharada Devi. In 1901 AD, he started a school at Shantiniketan which was later converted into a University named as Vishva Bharti in 1921 AD. In 1913 A.D. Tagore was awarded with Nobel Prize for literature for his literacy works like - 'Song Offerings', the English translation of his collection of poems ‘Gitanjali’. He was called as the Great sentinel by Gandhiji. Gandhiji believed that Rabindranath Tagore emphasized on moral forces for the freedom struggle.
The famous slogan of Jai Jawan Jai Kisan was given by former P.M. of India Lal Bahadur Shastri .

During भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन [Quit India Movement] Movement which was started on 9 August 1942 AD Gandhiji said that Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight. Gandhi gave the mantra- 'Do or Die' We shall either free India or die in the attempt.
Jawaharlal Nehru post-Independence said that everything could wait but not the agriculture.
Mountbatten blamed Jinnah for India’s partition.
In August 1923 AD, the session of All India Hindu Mahasabha at Banaras was chaired by Madan Mohan Malviya. It was attended by 1500 delegates from various religions such as Hindu, Sikhs, Parsis, etc.

Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) born at Utmanzai (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan), Frontier Tribal area of early British India is also known as Bacha Khan, Fakhr-e-Afghan etc. He was awarded Bharat Ratna in 1987 AD.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors *Annie Besant founded Central Hindu College in 1898 AD and was elected as the President (International) of the Theosophical Society in 1907 AD . She founded a weekly newspaper 'Commonweal' in January 1914 for her political work. In June 1914 she purchased the 'Madras Standard' and renamed it 'New India', which thereafter became her chosen organ for her tempestuous propaganda for India's freedom. * Lieutenant Colonel James Tod in his book 'Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan' wrote about the feudal system of Rajasthan. * Shyamji Krishna Verma was an Indian revolutionary and journalist who published journal ‘The Indian Sociologist'. *Amar Sonar Bangla was composed in 1905 during the partition of Bengal by Rabindranath Tagore. The melody (tune) of this song were inspired by Harkara's ‘ Ami Kothay Pabo Tare’ song of Gagan Harkara. First ten lines of the song Amar Sonar Bangla were adopted as National Anthem of Bangladesh ofﬁ cially in 1972 AD. This song was translated into English by ‘Syed Ali Ahsan’ . Rabindranath Tagore composed Jan-Gan-Mana too. He is the only poet credited with authoring the national anthems of two countries. The Bengali edition of Gitanjali was published on 14 August 1910 (31 Shravan 1317). Its English edition was published for the ﬁ rst time in November 1912 AD. Rabindranath Tagore won the 1913 Nobel Prize in literature; Gitanjali: Song Offerings was the english book chieﬂ y associated with the award, and it was Tagore's own English selection/recasting of the Bengali Gitanjali (version) alone (not direct translation of the book only). Deliberative book “Hind Swaraj” was ﬁ rstly published in Gujarati in 1909 AD. British Government censored this book. In March 1910, the Bombay Government proscribed its circulation; Gandhi then published his own English rendering, Indian होम रूल आंदोलन [Home Rule Movement], in reply. In this book, Gandhiji compared British Parliament to a sterile women and a prostitute and commented on working processes of the British Government. "Gokhale : My Political Guru, a book was ﬁ rst published in February, 1955 by Navajivan Publishing House, Ahmedabad. The book is an English compilation of Gandhi's earlier writings and speeches on Gokhale". *Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (1820-1891 AD) was a great social reformer and educationist of the 19th century. Primarily by his efforts the Hindu Widows Remarriage Act, 1856 was passed. He wrote ‘Bahuvivah’ and ‘Balya Vivaher Dosh’ . *‘Das Kapital’ was written by famous German socialist Karl Marx. In this book he straight away criticized the capitalism and presented his Socialist principles which are also known as Marxism (like inquiry into the laws of motion of modern society). First part of the book was published during the lifetime of Marx whereas the second and third part of the book was edited and published by his friend and associate Friedrich Engels. * ‘Anand Math’ of Bankimchandra Chatterjee is considered as the Bible of Bengali patriotism. This Book is based on the Sanyasi Revolt (1763-1800 AD). *Kesari Singh Barhath was poet and freedom ﬁ ghter of Rajasthan. In 1903, he wrote ‘Chetavani-Ra-Chungatya’ having 13 soratha/couplets. *Maithili Sharan गुप्त साम्राज्य [Gupta Empire] is a famous poet adorned with the title of ‘National Poet’. He is the writer of 'Bharat Bharti'. His other works include Panchavati, Saket, Yashodhara, Jayadrath Vadh etc. *'Ae Mere Watan ke logo' a patriotic song is written by Pradeep. Born in a small town Badnagar with in the Ujjain district, Madhya Pradesh the real name of Pradeep was Ram Chandra Narayanji Dwivedi. He wrote a condolence song on the martyrs of 1962 AD Indo-China war. The music of this song was composed by C. Ramchandra. *Md. Iqbal was born on 9 November 1877 AD at Sialkot in Punjab of British India. The famous poet of Urdu and advocate by profession Iqbal was a nationalist from the beginning. He wrote - ‘Sare Jahan se Accha Hindostan Hamara’ but later on he joined Muslim League. ‘Majhab Nahi Sikhata apas me bair Rakhna’ is a line from the Song Sare Jahan se Accha by Iqbal. *‘Landmarks in Indian Constitutional and National Development’ was written by writer Gurumukh Nihal Singh. He was the Governor of Rajasthan from 1956 to 1962 AD. * G.A. Natesan was the editor of the book 'Congress Presidential Addresses' (1934-35 AD). This book was published in two parts. The ﬁ rst one contained the congress Presidential Addresses from 1885 to 1910, and the other one contained the same from 1911 AD to 1934 AD. *Jawaharlal Nehru when he was jailed at Ahmednagar Fort (1942-1945 AD) wrote a book named The Discovery of India. Also, in his jail term, Nehru wrote an Autobiography (also known as Toward Freedom) and Glimpses of World History (in 1930s). *Sachindranath Sanyal wrote ‘Bandi Jeevan’. *‘A Journey through the Kingdom of Oude in 1849-50’ report was written by W.H. Sleeman and published in two volumes in London. *‘JP Movement-Emergency and India' Second Freedom' was a book written by M.G. Devasahayam . *Lieutenant General Brij Mohan Kaul wrote the book ‘The Untold Story’. This book was published in 1967 AD and throws light on India-China war of 1962 AD. *Hans Christian Andersen in his writings wrote about fairy tales. His important works are : The Steadfast Tin Soldier, The Snow Queen, The Little Mermaid, Thumbelina etc. *'The Golden Gate' published in 1986 AD is the ﬁ rst novel by Vikram Seth. * Rachel Carson wrote ‘Silent Spring’. She was a famous American Biologist. In this book, questions are raised about the use of pesticides. *‘The Satanic Verses’ is the fourth novel of Salman Rushdie. Its ﬁ rst publication took place in 1988 AD. This book was in the news for some time regarding various controversies. Rushdie's ﬁ rst published novel 'Grimus', appeared in 1975. * 'The Namesake' was the ﬁ rst novel of Jhumpa Lahiri. Jhumpa Lahiri is a Pulitzer Prize winner.
